eligibility.quote: If launching the same node with pixel_format ="mjpeg" the terminal outputs a continuing stream of these warnings: [swscaler @ 0x1545460] deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly

failed_conditions.quote: [swscaler @ 0x1545460] deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly

loudness.quote: the terminal outputs a continuing stream of these warnings: [swscaler @ 0x1545460] deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly

resolution.quote: Suppress warnings of the form: [swscaler @ 0x############] deprecated pixel format used, make sure you did set range correctly ... This warning can be safely ignored at present.

notes: Issue body verbatim confirms the warning stream and that frames otherwise work ('the frames seem to be captured normally otherwhise, and the live image works fine'). Eligibility is a documented judgment call the spec itself flags: the offending full-range YUVJ pixel-format value is produced by FFmpeg's own decoder and consumed by FFmpeg's scaler, with usb_cam passing it through unchanged; the spec treats FFmpeg as one provider unit and usb_cam as the consumer passing the value across the boundary. This is defensible but borderline (an adjudicator treating decoder+scaler as the real composition would call it internal to FFmpeg). outcome warning_only, loudness loud_documented (provider library emits the diagnostic, detection_stage run), and resolution recommended (PR #115 merged to develop 37451954 suppresses the warning; no resolved composition with an identified FFmpeg revision is shown) are all correct.
